answer: A cipher bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent identity must lock a refundable stake in shared escrow before it can transact, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs thousands of stakes. Like a pearl forming only around a genuine grain of sand, reputation accrues slowly per identity - crystal-clear on-ledger history of completed work - and a fresh identity with no history cannot command the same trust or fees as an established one. Attackers pay real capital per identity while honest agents earn it back, so each fake identity costs more than it can extract.
